x: Baulch especially was in fine fettle to finish 11th behind such names as Firth, Caulder, Barrett, Towl, Maynard, Clark and Driver, all of whom are in international class in one sphere or another.
Mike Maynard set a fast pace at the start and was comfortably leading after a mile from John Moore and Chris Thompson with Clive Shippen and the Blackheath captain, A.W.

At two miles, with Maynard(H.H.H.) leading from Eldon and Knight, Pat was 15th, John 46th and our sixth scoring man in the nineties. At six miles, Eldon had established a substantial lead from Knight and Sando with Maynard 4th.

Jim Radford was a very good second to Maynard (HHH) in the 1½ miles; third place going to Charlie Dabbs, now free from injury. Eric Penny gained a valuable 10 points with a win in the junior ¾ mile, and a walk-over in the 660 yards.

…company in his coach - Hyman, Peter Cl[illegible]rk, Brian Fernee, Chapman, Roath, Perkins, Mike Barratt, George Brown, Maynard, Palmer and Sando just to mention a few are not designed to rouse one's confidence.…
Everything depended on Don Maclean over the last stage and no-one envied him his task--Maynard of Cambridge H. 46seconds ahead and Malcolm Browne, the Essex Beagle miler, just 20seconds behind.

Individual wins were recorded by Ernie Obeng 100m, Marcus Adam 200m, Stu Paton 1500m, Mike Hayes 3000 S/C, Femi Abejide Triple Jump and Nigel Bevan, Javelin Throw and the 4x400m Relay Team of Cuff, Busk, Maynard and Paton.
Darryl Maynard had a fine debut in the 'A' 800m. Ossie Cham made an impressive entrance with a brilliant 2.10m for 2nd place in the High Jump being ably backed up by Leroy Haughton.
Schloss Maynard 86. Top of the list at Waitrose for past few years.
